question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3 \\ 6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $-4a+\frac{b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}54 & -18 \\ -18 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & -9 \\ -18 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{9}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{6} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-4a+\frac{b}{c}=-4\cdot (-\frac{1}{6})+\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{1}=1.
$$
